answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud or duplicate claims. Auditors check signed task receipts against a public ledger; a cipher can bind each receipt to its submitter, while a marble-sized deposit is still costly if an attacker must fund thousands of identities. Honest agents recover stake, but Sybils risk losing capital and must keep replacing it, making scale expensive rather than merely a meadow of cheap accounts.
